prolate_spheroidal.label: The axis, $q = 1$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $x$ ($y = 1$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = 1$, $m = 1$). The metric on it is $-e^{2\psi}c^2dt^2 + m^2e^{-2\psi}dx^2$ with $e^{2\psi} = f^{(3x^2 + 1)/2}e^{3x}$ and $f = (x - 1)/(x + 1)$, so a ray has $c\,dt/dx = \pm m\,e^{-2\psi}$, and every rotation about the axis fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.

The cones close as $(x - 1)^2$ toward $x = 1$, which a ray reaches only as $t \to \pm\infty$, though after a finite affine distance, since $x$ is an affine parameter along it. The Kretschmann scalar stays finite on the axis and is $3e^6/(4m^4)$ at $x = 1$.

prolate_spheroidal.label: The equatorial plane, $q = 1$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $x$ ($y = 0$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = 1$, $m = 1$). A ray has $c\,dt/dx = \pm m\,x\,e^{\gamma - 2\psi}/\sqrt{x^2 - 1}$, and the reflection $y \to -y$ fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.

The cones close toward $x = 1$, where $c\,dt/dx$ grows as $(x - 1)^{-7/8}$, so every ingoing ray reaches it in a finite time $t$. The Kretschmann scalar diverges there as $(x - 1)^{-3/2}$ and the circles about the axis shrink to zero.

prolate_spheroidal.label: The axis, $q = -1/2$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $x$ ($y = 1$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = -1/2$, $m = 1$). The metric on it is $-e^{2\psi}c^2dt^2 + m^2e^{-2\psi}dx^2$ with $e^{2\psi} = f^{(5 - 3x^2)/4}e^{-3x/2}$ and $f = (x - 1)/(x + 1)$, so a ray has $c\,dt/dx = \pm m\,e^{-2\psi}$, and every rotation about the axis fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.
The cones close as $(x - 1)^{1/2}$ toward $x = 1$, which every ingoing ray reaches in a finite time $t$ and where the Kretschmann scalar on the axis diverges as $(x - 1)^{-3}$.

prolate_spheroidal.label: The equatorial plane, $q = -1/2$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $x$ ($y = 0$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = -1/2$, $m = 1$). A ray has $c\,dt/dx = \pm m\,x\,e^{\gamma - 2\psi}/\sqrt{x^2 - 1}$, and the reflection $y \to -y$ fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.

The cones close toward $x = 1$, where $c\,dt/dx$ grows as $(x - 1)^{-31/32}$: an ingoing ray reaches it in a finite time $t$, and light from $x = 1.1$ takes $70\,m/c$ to do so. The Kretschmann scalar diverges there as $(x - 1)^{-21/8}$ and the circles about the axis grow without bound.

spherical.label: The axis, $q = 1$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $r$ ($\theta = 0$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = 1$, $m = 1$). The metric on it is $-e^{2\psi}c^2dt^2 + e^{-2\psi}dr^2$ with $e^{2\psi} = f^{(3x^2 + 1)/2}e^{3x}$, $f = 1 - 2m/r$, and $x = r/m - 1$, so a ray has $c\,dt/dr = \pm e^{-2\psi}$, and every rotation about the axis fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.

The cones close as $(r - 2m)^2$ toward $r = 2m$, which a ray reaches only as $t \to \pm\infty$, though after a finite affine distance, since $r$ is an affine parameter along it. The Kretschmann scalar stays finite on the axis and is $3e^6/(4m^4)$ at $r = 2m$.

spherical.label: The equatorial plane, $q = 1$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = 1$, $m = 1$). A ray has $c\,dt/dr = \pm (r - m)\,e^{\gamma - 2\psi}/\sqrt{r^2 - 2mr}$, and the reflection $\theta \to \pi - \theta$ fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.

The cones close toward $r = 2m$, where $c\,dt/dr$ grows as $(r - 2m)^{-7/8}$, so every ingoing ray reaches it in a finite time $t$. The Kretschmann scalar diverges there as $(r - 2m)^{-3/2}$ and the circles about the axis shrink to zero.

The cones close as $(r - 2m)^{1/2}$ toward $r = 2m$, which every ingoing ray reaches in a finite time $t$ and where the Kretschmann scalar on the axis diverges as $(r - 2m)^{-3}$.

spherical.label: The equatorial plane, $q = -1/2$
caption: The plane of $t$ and $r$ ($\theta = \pi/2$, $\phi = 0$) of the Erez-Rosen metric ($q = -1/2$, $m = 1$). A ray has $c\,dt/dr = \pm (r - m)\,e^{\gamma - 2\psi}/\sqrt{r^2 - 2mr}$, and the reflection $\theta \to \pi - \theta$ fixes the plane, so the rays are null geodesics.
